parameters.content:
## Meeting Prep Workflow

Starter template from agentmelt.com — configure before running:

1. Fill in "Config (edit me)" (name, approver, quiet hours; test_mode stays on for the first week).
2. Add credentials to every service node (Anthropic, mail, CRM, database…).
3. Replace placeholder URLs, queries and field mappings with yours.
4. Set the trigger: Google or Microsoft calendar scanned for meetings with external attendees in the next 24 hours; new bookings via webhook.
5. Keep the gates: 'Needs a person?' after every AI step, 'Approved?' after the approval — wire their dead ends to a sheet or a channel.
6. Keep the guardrails:
   - Only public and first-party data; no scraping behind logins, no personal data beyond professional role.
   - Every statement in the brief carries a source; the agent is instructed to omit rather than guess.
   - Briefs go only to the rep and the CRM; they are not forwarded externally.
   - Enrichment credits are spent only for meetings that survive the external-attendee filter.

Full blueprint and pricing: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/meeting-prep-research/
Want it built and run for you? $197/month · custom $2,000–3,500 one-time

nodes.name: Config (edit me)
nodes.notes:
Fill these in once; every later node reads them as $('Config (edit me)').item.json.config.*

test_mode = true: log what the workflow would write, without writing it, for the first week.
approval_mode = true: the approval node waits for a person; switch off per message type once it has earned it.

Also point the nodes at your own sources:
- Calendar (Google Workspace, Microsoft 365)
- CRM (HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive)
- Enrichment and news (Clay, Apollo, Clearbit, news APIs)
- Product usage / billing for existing accounts

options.systemMessage:
You are the "Write the brief" step of the Meeting Prep Workflow workflow run by Agentmelt.
Task: One page: company in two lines, what changed recently, attendees and roles, relationship history and open items, live account signals, and three suggested angles tied to the evidence. Nothing without a source.

Rules:
- Only public and first-party data; no scraping behind logins, no personal data beyond professional role.
- Every statement in the brief carries a source; the agent is instructed to omit rather than guess.
- Briefs go only to the rep and the CRM; they are not forwarded externally.
- Enrichment credits are spent only for meetings that survive the external-attendee filter.
- Answer only from the data provided in the input. If something is missing, say so in the output instead of guessing.
- If this step produces a message or a document, put the full text in `draft` (and a `subject` if it is an email); put a one-line summary in `summary`.
- Set `needs_human` true whenever you are unsure, the input is unusual, or a rule above applies; a person will look at it.
- Return valid JSON matching the output schema; no prose outside the JSON.

nodes.name: AI Agent: Write the brief
nodes.notes:
Write the brief

One page: company in two lines, what changed recently, attendees and roles, relationship history and open items, live account signals, and three suggested angles tied to the evidence. Nothing without a source.

nodes.name: Needs a person?
nodes.notes: True = the AI step was not sure or flagged the item → dead letter, a person looks. False = continue. Wire the dead letter to a Slack message or a sheet so nothing fails silently.

nodes.name: Needs a person: Write the brief
nodes.notes: Dead letter. Replace this no-op with a Slack message or a sheet row that carries the raw item and the reason — silent failures are the ones that cost.

nodes.name: Slack: Deliver
nodes.notes:
Deliver

Posted as a DM to the rep an hour before, and attached to the calendar event and the CRM deal.

nodes.name: Wait: Capture the outcome
nodes.notes:
Capture the outcome

After the meeting a one-question prompt ('how did it go, next step?'); the answer is logged to the CRM so the next brief includes it.
